question: The first armed tribal rebellion against the British is considered to have taken place in:
solution:
The correct answer is __**1784**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The** first armed tribal rebellion** against British rule in India is considered to be the **Tamar Rebellion of 1784**.
 
• This rebellion was led by the **Tamar tribe** in the Chotanagpur region (present-day Jharkhand).
 
• The Tamar tribes revolted against the exploitative policies of the British, especially related to land revenue and forced labor.
 
• It marked the beginning of resistance movements by tribal communities, which continued with uprisings like the Kol Rebellion (1831) and the Santhal Rebellion (1855).
 
• Tribal resistance was fueled by the disruption of traditional lifestyles, exploitation by landlords, and the introduction of new laws and systems by the British administration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tamar Rebellion:**

 
 
• It was one of the earliest tribal revolts in India, occurring in 1784.
 
• The rebellion was triggered by the British policies of heavy taxation and forced labor (begar).
 
• The leaders of the rebellion used traditional tribal warfare tactics against the British forces.
 
 
 
• **Kol Rebellion (1831-1832):**
 
 
• Led by the Kol tribes in the Chotanagpur region.
 
• It was an uprising against the British and moneylenders who exploited tribal land and resources.
 
 
 
• **Santhal Rebellion (1855-1856):**
 
 
• Also known as the Santhal Hul, this revolt was led by Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu.
 
• The Santhals revolted against the oppressive policies of the British and the zamindars.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Tribal Revolts:**
 
 
• These uprisings highlighted the plight of tribal communities under British rule.
 
• They are significant for understanding the early resistance movements in India.
